I am thinking about this year's planting. My 3.5 mu is not much, but it feeds part of our family of 7, and with some of us working outside, I cannot waste money on the land either.

Last year my wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, and maize around 550 kg per mu. That is normal for our area in Quzhou. I will do about the same this year — what works, I keep.

For wheat, I plant in October. I use improved seed from the agro-shop, the kind most neighbors here use — I think it is Jimai variety. I buy compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind) as base, about 50 kg per mu before sowing with the rotary tiller. Then at jointing in spring I topdress urea, maybe 20 kg per mu. So nitrogen comes to around 17 kg N per mu, phosphorus and potassium 7-8 kg each. I irrigate at sowing, before winter, at jointing, and at grain-filling — 4 times from the well. Pesticide I spray twice, once for aphids and once with the herbicide.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June — hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the dealer pushes that year. Maize eats more nitrogen. I put compound fertilizer at sowing, maybe 40 kg per mu, then urea at big trumpet stage, 25 kg. That gives about 20 kg N. I do no-tillage for maize, just drill into the wheat stubble — saves time and diesel. Irrigate 2-3 times if the rain is short. Spray once for corn borer.

I don't want to cut fertilizer and lose yield — a bad harvest hurts much more than spending a few hundred yuan extra on urea.
